newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Vandals deface Rio church being cleaned for pope.
newsitem.headline: Vandals deface Rio church being cleaned for pope.

text.p: Seven weeks before Pope John Paul is to visit the city, vandals sprayed graffiti inside Candelaria, one of Rio de Janeiro's best-loved churches, the police said on Monday.
A police spokesman said three people, probably adolescents, were seen clambering up scaffolding on the front of the church in the early hours of Sunday.
The vandals climbed into the church through the bell tower and sprayed colored paint on the ceiling and on a 19th-century Carrara marble statue called "The Fall of the Cherubs."
The scaffolding was installed so the church facade could be cleaned before the Pope's visit to Rio from Oct. 2 to 5.
"This incident demonstrates immoral behavior that defies even the most basic common sense," Rio de Janeiro Archbishop Dom Eugenio Sales said in a statement.
It was at Candelaria, in central Rio, that military police gunned down eight sleeping street children in 1993.
